messages:
alex.s (Sales): Hey team, Pioneer POC is seeing big variability in TTFT and intermittent 429s during peak replay tests. Sam, can you paste a short timeline? :wave:

sam.t (Pioneer): Started 10:00 UTC running parallel load (50 concurrent small prompts). Around run 3 we saw spikes, a bunch of 429s and some first-byte lag.

maya.s (Solutions): Thanks. Do you have recent request IDs or a sample log? Also which model variant and whether you're using prefill/prefix caching?

sam.t (Pioneer): Model: redwood/medium-v2, no explicit prefill. Using SDK default batching. Request IDs: r-9764, r-9765, r-9766. Here's a small snippet from our client logs:

```
2026-03-21T10:03:12Z INFO request=r-9764 status=queued queue_ms=120
2026-03-21T10:03:12Z WARN request=r-9764 backend=busy backpressure=true
2026-03-21T10:03:13Z ERROR request=r-9764 code=429 reason="rate_limit"
```

jordan.o (Oncall): That backpressure flag usually means queue saturation on the shard. Could be due to continuous batching window being too long or shard qps limits. Lee, any recent routing changes?

lee.r (Runtime): No routing changes. Observed the same on infra metrics: per-shard inflight jumped and we hit soft rlimit which yields 429. Two quick suspects: (1) client is sending bursts that trigger queue-affinity shuffling, causing batch fragmentation; (2) KV cache miss rate is high so tokens cost more and throughput drops.

maya.s (Solutions): Sam, can you confirm typical sequence length and if you see many unique prompts? If cache miss rate is high, prefill helps. Also check SDK prefetch settings (concurrency and batch_max_tokens).

sam.t (Pioneer): Seq len ~60 avg, prompts are fairly similar but we did churn some dynamic context. We didn't enable any prefill/prefix caching.

alex.s (Sales): Quick commercial question: if we recommend prefill or Dedicated during POC, what's the cost delta and how do we convey that to Pioneer? Carla?

carla.a (Account): For bursts like this: Hosted cost vs Dedicated: hosted burst pricing may spike due to per-token + queue overhead. Dedicated (reserved vGPU pools) gives predictable throughput and avoids soft rlimits, but needs commitment. I'll DM a sample comparison chart. Short answer: expected unit cost up during wasted requeues; Dedicated reduces that variability.

jordan.o (Oncall): For immediate mitigation, try these steps: 1) Reduce client concurrency to 20 and enable SDK prefetch=2. 2) Set batch_max_tokens=256 and batch_window_ms=20. 3) Enable prefix prefill for the common prompt part.

lee.r (Runtime): Adding: If you can share 10 representative prompts we can run a quantized warmup (kv prefetch) on the model shard. Also enable request-level route hinting to prefer low-latency shard (header: X-Redwood-Route: fast).

sam.t (Pioneer): Ok I'll try those now. One more: we filled security questionnaire; any blockers re: logging retention and PII?

alex.s (Sales): Security doc submitted last week. Maya / Security team to confirm.

maya.s (Solutions): For logs: we can redact PII at ingestion and only forward request IDs. Retention is configurable—standard 30 days for hosted. For enterprise, Private deployment supports stricter retention and local logs.

sam.t (Pioneer): Update: after lowering concurrency and enabling prefill, 429 rate dropped but TTFT still spikes on a few requests. Attaching a new log run (r-9788..r-9795).

```
2026-03-21T10:15:01Z INFO request=r-9790 status=started first_byte_ms=420
2026-03-21T10:15:01Z INFO request=r-9792 status=started first_byte_ms=138
2026-03-21T10:15:02Z INFO request=r-9789 status=started first_byte_ms=395
```

lee.r (Runtime): Those first_byte_ms outliers (>=400ms) are likely caused by shard cold-path due to KV cache miss. We saw higher miss-rate spikes at 10:00-10:20. I'll trigger a targeted warmup (prefill) on the affected shard. ETA ~10 minutes.

jordan.o (Oncall): I'll keep monitoring. If TTFT stays bad after warmup, we'll look at increasing max_inflight on the shard temporarily (requires ops approval).

carla.a (Account): Sam, if you want to avoid ops interventions during POC, we can flip a temporary Dedicated trial for a day—gives consistent throughput. I can scope pricing; need approval from Pioneer.

sam.t (Pioneer): Please send details. For now warmup sounds fine. Also, is there a recommended SDK config we can bake into our deployment to avoid this in prod?

maya.s (Solutions): Recommended defaults for similar workloads: concurrency=16, prefetch=2, batch_max_tokens=256, batch_window_ms=15-25, enable prefix prefill for common context. Also instrument request_id propagation so we can correlate logs.

alex.s (Sales): Great. Actions: Lee to run warmup; Jordan to monitor; Maya to send recommended SDK snippet and a one‑pager on prefill; Carla to send Dedicated trial pricing; Sam to confirm whether Pioneer wants trial. Everyone OK? :thumbsup:

lee.r (Runtime): Warmup started on shard s-17.

deploy-bot: warmup job job-443 queued -> running on s-17

jordan.o (Oncall): Metrics look better now, first_byte median down to ~120ms, 429s rare. I'll leave a 1-hour watch.

sam.t (Pioneer): Seeing much better numbers. Thanks all. Carla, please send trial details and Maya, I need that SDK snippet.

maya.s (Solutions): Sending SDK snippet and prefill how-to in #eng-docs shortly. Snippet: ```js
client.generate({prefill: true, concurrency:16, prefetch:2, batch: {max_tokens:256, window_ms:20}})
```

carla.a (Account): I'll email Pioneer the Dedicated 24-hour trial proposal + cost delta spreadsheet.

alex.s (Sales): Closing loop — will follow up on acceptance. Nice cross-team response :clap:

sam.t (Pioneer): Appreciate the fast help, team.
